channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula: A gente vai demorar muito para fazer tudo porque partimos do nada
item.description: President Lula stated that the Brazilian elite never cared about literacy for workers and that solving inequalities in Brazil is a slow process. He emphasized that the country starts from scratch to advance social transformations.

item.title: Caiado acusa Lula e Flávio de envolvimento com Vorcaro; Zema diz querer ministros do STF presos
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado accused Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro of involvement with Daniel Vorcaro and corruption cases during a debate hosted by Veja. Romeu Zema stated he wants Supreme Court justices arrested if Lula or Flávio win.

item.title: Caiado critica penduricalhos em reforma administrativa; Zema ataca número de ministérios
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) advocated for an administrative reform that eliminates 'frills' and reduces excessive spending in the public sector during a debate promoted by Veja. Romeu Zema (Novo) also supported a leaner government, criticizing the existence of 38 ministries in the current federal structure.

item.title: Em debate do Estadão, candidatos ao Senado criticam Alcolumbre e cobram impeachment do STF
item.description: Senate candidates from São Paulo, André do Prado (PL) and Guilherme Derrite (PP), supported the impeachment of Supreme Court justices and criticized Davi Alcolumbre during a debate with Estadão and FAAP.

item.title: Lula defende emenda constitucional para transformar centralidade da Cultura em cláusula pétrea
item.description: Lula proposed a constitutional amendment to make cultural centrality a constitutional clause, during an event with artists in Rio.

item.title: Caiado compara voto em Lula ou Flávio Bolsonaro a ‘jogar no tigrinho’: ‘Você já perdeu’
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) compared voting for Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro to playing 'tigrinho', claiming the voter has already lost. He labeled the matchup as 'Russian roulette' and advocated for alternatives, citing his personal trajectory as an example of life.

item.title: Lula diz que está ganhando de Trump em disputa de narrativas
item.description: President Lula claimed he is winning a narrative battle against Donald Trump, contrasting Brazil's rhetoric with Trump's focus on military strength at the UN. He criticized Trump's threatening tone and used a cultural event in Rio to rally support among artists.

item.title: Quem são os candidatos a deputado federal pela Bahia (BA) nas eleições 2026
item.description: Over 11.3 million voters are eligible to vote for 535 candidates for federal deputy in Bahia in the 2026 elections. The state will elect 39 parliamentarians, using the proportional system for the Chamber of Deputies. The election takes place on October 4th, with a single round.

item.title: Lula aciona TSE e STF por suposto apoio estrangeiro a campanha de Flávio
item.description: Lula files lawsuits with TSE and STF against Flávio Bolsonaro, Alfredo Gaspar and Eduardo Bolsonaro over alleged immigrant vote-baiting and campaign ad violations. The complaints also challenge alleged foreign support for Flávio's campaign.

item.title: Campanha de Lula vai ao TSE contra Flávio por suposta interferência estrangeira na eleição
item.description: Lula's campaign filed a lawsuit with the TSE accusing Flávio Bolsonaro, Eduardo Bolsonaro, and Alfredo Gaspar of alleged foreign interference, with support from Donald Trump, in the 2026 election. The petition highlights an 'external intervention infrastructure' involving communication, institutions, and diplomacy, focusing on the Rockbridge Network and disinformation via social media. The PT demands investigations, testimonies, and access to big tech data.

item.title: Quaest no Tocantins: Lula, 37%; Flávio Bolsonaro, 35%
item.description: In a Quaest poll of 804 voters in Tocantins, Lula leads with 37% over Flávio Bolsonaro at 35%. In a hypothetical runoff, both candidates tie at 44%.

item.title: “Globo” manterá debate mesmo sem Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: TV Globo confirmed it will hold the October 1st presidential debate even if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) do not participate. With the fragmentation of right-wing candidates, Lula becomes a target of criticism as the incumbent, while Flávio maintains he will not debate without the petista. Their absences have already led Record and Band to cancel debates scheduled for September 27th and August 23rd.

item.title: PT pede ao STF abertura de inquérito sobre possível interferência estrangeira na eleição
item.description: The PT requested the STF to open an investigation into potential foreign interference in the election, citing cases like the Rockbridge Network and suspicious funding. Lula's campaign also questioned Flávio Bolsonaro and allies at the TSE, accusing them of power abuse and coordination with the US government.

item.title: Lula se reúne com artistas na Lapa, Rio, na reta final da campanha
item.description: President Lula attended an event with artists and cultural figures at Fundição Progresso in Lapa, Rio, as part of his re-election campaign, 11 days before the first round. The gathering included personalities such as Chico Buarque, Paulinho da Viola and Daniela Mercury, along with authorities like First Lady Janja and Minister of Culture Margareth Menezes.

item.title: TSE julga recurso contra candidatura de Dr Furlan, líder nas pesquisa ao governo do AP
item.description: The TSE will rule on Thursday (Sept 24) on a motion seeking to disqualify Dr Furlan (PSD) from running for governor of Amapá, after the Public Ministry argued he circumvented the Clean Record Act by resigning after a corruption complaint.

item.title: Lula reage, e empate mineiro mantém eleição aberta; leia análise de Felipe Nunes
item.description: Quaest polls in Minas Gerais and São Paulo show Lula tied numerically with Flávio Bolsonaro in the second round, both reaching 40%. Lula advances in the first round in Minas Gerais, from 31% to 35%, while government approval rises from 41% to 44% in the state.

item.title: Meta Connect 2026: Zuckerberg apresenta novos óculos inteligentes; acompanhe
item.description: Meta executives Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang unveiled new smart glasses, AI agents, and tools for Instagram, WhatsApp, and Facebook, promoting an optimistic view of technology with minimal regulation. The company faced criticism over insufficient safeguards against deepfakes and privacy concerns, yet launched paid subscriptions in Brazil and partnerships with companies like Wallmart and Best Buy. Zuckerberg emphasized smart glasses as the leading wearable category in the AI era, highlighting voice features, real-time translation, and encryption.

item.title: Ala do STF leva luta pelo poder disputada nas urnas para dentro da Corte
item.description: The Supreme Court quadrumvirate, aligned with Lula, merged the institutional crisis with the elections, turning it into a struggle for power within the Court. The hardline faction used coercion and pressure, tying its fate to the electoral outcome, but underestimated widespread distrust of the judiciary. The crisis exposes a collapsing patronage cycle worsened by leadership vacuum, threatening institutional stability.

item.title: Quaest: após novo recuo em MG, Zema vê Cury e Caiado à frente e já é quinto colocado no estado que governou
item.description: A new Quaest poll shows that Romeu Zema (Novo) secured only 2% of voting intentions in Minas Gerais, dropping to fifth place, overtaken by leaders such as Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, Augusto Curi, and Ronaldo Caiado. In other regions like São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, Zema also shows weak performance with 1% support. The poll indicates a significant decline from his base as governor of Minas Gerais.

item.title: Lula aciona TSE contra possível financiamento dos EUA a Flávio
item.description: Lula's campaign files a lawsuit with the TSE to investigate potential U.S. funding for Flávio Bolsonaro, requesting transparency regarding the source of funds and foreign interference in the 2026 election. The request seeks clarification on possible foreign involvement and improper electoral benefits in the Brazilian electoral process.

item.title: Campanha de Lula aciona STF e TSE por possível interferência dos EUA nas eleições
item.description: President Lula's campaign filed a lawsuit with the STF and TSE to investigate possible U.S. interference in the Brazilian electoral process. The action seeks urgent measures to investigate alleged foreign actions that could impact the country's electoral sovereignty.

item.title: ‘É deprimente’, diz Caiado sobre os candidatos ausentes no debate de VEJA com presidenciáveis
item.description: Caiado criticizes the absence of candidates in the VEJA debate, calling the situation depressing. Zema and Caiado participated in the event, while Lula, Flávio Bolsonaro, and others declined the invitation. The absence of main candidates is seen as a shielding strategy against attacks.

item.title: Marília tem 18% e Humberto, 14%, na disputa pelo Senado em PE
item.description: A Quaest poll released on September 23, 2026 shows Marília Arraes (PDT) leading with 18% of voting intentions in the Senate race in Pernambuco, followed by Humberto Costa (PT) with 14%. Since two senators are elected per state, respondents chose for both seats, totaling 100%. The survey interviewed 1,302 people between September 19 and 22, has a margin of error of 3 points, and was registered with the TSE.

item.title: Quaest: Flávio sobe, mas segue empatado tecnicamente Lula em SP no 1º turno
item.description: A new Quaest poll in São Paulo shows a technical tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round, with 34% and 31% respectively. In a potential second round, Flávio leads with 42% against 36% for Lula. The survey, with a 2-point margin of error, was conducted between September 19 and 22 with 1,800 voters.

item.title: Os detalhes da nova pesquisa Datafolha, a 10 dias da eleição presidencial
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll, released 10 days before the 2026 presidential election, shows Lula at 46% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 44% in the projected second round. The previous edition had Lula leading with 39% in the first round, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 36%. The institute will also release gubernatorial voting intentions for five states.

item.title: STF mantém aumento de custas judiciais no ES de até R$ 98 mil
item.description: The Brazilian Supreme Federal Court (STF) upheld updated judicial fee regulations in Espírito Santo, allowing fees of up to R$98,000 after 2026 adjustments. Justice Cármen Lúcia ruled against the OAB's challenge, deeming the fees proportional for court operations. Justices Flávio Dino and Gilmar Mendes opposed the decision, arguing the fees remain excessively high.

item.title: Por que governo Lula vê 'cavalo de Troia' em ação coordenada dos EUA e mais 14 países contra facções como PCC e CV
item.description: The Lula administration criticizes the coordinated action of the US and 14 countries against factions like PCC and CV, seeing a 'Trojan horse' to increase US influence in the region.

item.title: Ao vivo: Flávio antecipa live semanal
item.description: Senator and presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) advanced his weekly live stream on YouTube to this Wednesday (23) at 7 PM. The broadcast has been conducted since July and follows the format used by his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: PT pede ao STF investigação sobre interferência estrangeira nas eleições
item.description: The PT requested the STF to open an investigation into possible foreign interference in the elections, including suspicions of external funding for Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign. The party asked for evidence preservation and identification of involved funders and beneficiaries. The request was sent to Minister Flávio Dino, rapporteur of ADPF 1.178.

item.title: Lula e Flávio empatam com 40% no 2º turno em MG, diz Quaest
item.description: A Quaest survey conducted between September 19 and 22, 2026 in Minas Gerais with 1,506 respondents and funded by Globo indicates a technical tie between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the projected second round, both with 40% of voting intentions, followed by blank/null/non-voters (13%) and undecideds (7%). In the first-round scenario, Lula leads with 35%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro with 30%, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points and a 95% confidence level.

item.title: TRE-PR mantém registro de Deltan Dallagnol
item.description: The Paraná State Electoral Court (TRE-PR) upheld the registration of Deltan Dallagnol's (Novo) Senate candidacy following a ruling on October 23. While the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) suspended his campaign activities due to legal concerns, the TRE-PR ruled that he remains eligible to run for the Senate seat.

item.title: Flávio seria favorito se eleição fosse hoje, diz Antonio Lavareda. Vídeo
item.description: Political scientist Antônio Lavareda states that Flávio Bolsonaro would be the front-runner if the presidential election were held today, despite being numerically tied with Lula in second-round projections. He emphasizes that higher abstention rates among low-income voters may harm Lula, as his voter base is more concentrated in that demographic. Lavareda also discusses Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes' stable approval rating, attributing it to perceptions of resistance against coup attempts and the Vorcaro scandal which diluted criticism toward the minister.

item.title: Lula tem 58% e Flávio, 25% no 2º turno em PE, diz Quaest
item.description: A Quaest survey released on September 23, 2026, shows President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) leading with 58% of voting intentions in a potential second-round matchup against Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), who holds 25%, among Pernambuco voters. Blank, null, and non-voters account for 12%, while 5% remain undecided. In the first round, Lula leads at 54%, followed by Flávio at 21%.

item.title: TSE exigirá de institutos mais detalhes sobre pesquisas eleitorais de 2º turno
item.description: The TSE will require polling institutes to provide more detailed information about electoral surveys for the second round of the 2026 elections, with an official communiqué expected to be issued soon by Chief Justice Kassio Nunes Marques.

item.title: Como foram discursos de Lula e Trump na Assembleia Geral da ONU
item.description: Lula and Trump spoke at the UN General Assembly in 2026, highlighting distinct positions on global issues. The live coverage was concluded after the speeches.

item.title: Sob Flávio, fim da reeleição virá quando o Saci cruzar as pernas
item.description: With 11 days left before the first round, Tarcísio de Freitas joined Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, recording a live video and advocating for the end of re-election. In return, Bolsonaro's son reiterated his stance against re-election. Their cooperation highlights strategic alliances in the electoral race.

item.title: No 2º turno do Rio, Flávio tem 44% e Lula, 36%; no 1º, senador marca 37%, segundo a Quaest
item.description: A new Quaest poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) with 44% of vote intentions in a potential runoff against Lula (PT), who has 36%, in Rio de Janeiro state elections. The survey also shows Flávio leading the race for state senator with 37%.

item.title: No 2º turno do DF, Flávio sobe de 45% a 49% e Lula mantém 38%, segundo a Quaest
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leads with 49% of vote intentions in a hypothetical runoff against Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), who has 38%, according to a Quaest poll in the Federal District. In the previous round, Flávio had 45% and Lula 38%.

item.title: No 2º turno de Pernambuco, Lula tem 58% e Flávio Bolsonaro soma 25%, aponta Quaest
item.description: In a hypothetical runoff in Pernambuco, Lula leads with 58% of voting intentions, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro with 25%, according to a Quaest survey. The poll shows stability in voting intentions, with minor changes from the previous round.

item.title: Números da pesquisa Quaest atualizam a corrida para o governo do Distrito Federal
item.description: A Quaest survey shows Celina Leão (PP) leading the gubernatorial race in the Federal District with 34% of voter intentions, followed by Leandro Grass (PT) with 23%. The candidacies of Arruda, Elisson, and Rico Pinheiro were rejected by the electoral court. In a simulated runoff, Celina leads Grass 48% to 30%.

item.title: Novas pesquisas mostram a distância entre Lula e Flávio nos três maiores colégios eleitorais do país
item.description: Quaest polls show Flávio Bolsonaro leading over Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, while tied in Minas Gerais. In São Paulo, Flávio reached 42% compared to Lula's 36%, with a two-point margin of error. The polls were commissioned by Globo and conducted between September 19 and 22.

item.title: Governo vê falha da campanha ao explicar relação de Lula com Moraes
item.description: Government officials criticize the campaign for failing to clearly explain the relationship between Lula and Moraes, allowing the STF crisis to reflect negatively on the president. They argue that any closeness between them stems from a shared threat during the coup attempt, but does not imply unconditional alliance in the Master case. The campaign's communication strategy was deemed ineffective for not contextualizing Moraes' political trajectory and the Senate rejection of his Supreme Court nominee.

item.title: OAB pede a Fachin sigilo de conversas entre investigados e advogados
item.description: The OAB requested the STF to preserve attorney-client privilege in materials seized by the Federal Police in the Compliance Zero operation, which investigates the Banco Master case, after conversations between Daniel Vorcaro and lawyers became public. The entity does not question the legality of the investigated conduct but defends that confidential information unrelated to the investigation should not be disclosed. The Presidency denied that Lula received gifts or messages from Vorcaro.

item.title: Lula x Bolsonaro: como ficou a votação em São Paulo no primeiro turno de 2022
item.description: In the first round of 2022, Jair Bolsonaro (PL) led the votes in São Paulo with 47.71%, against 40.89% for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). However, in the capital, Lula outperformed Bolsonaro, while the latter won most cities in the interior. In the second round, the trend continued: Bolsonaro expanded his state advantage, but Lula retained the lead in the capital.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula promove ato com artistas na Fundição Progresso, no Rio
item.description: President Lula participates in campaign events in Rio de Janeiro, including an artistic event at Fundição Progresso with Caetano Veloso, Chico Buarque and Maria Bethânia. He also holds an event with health workers.

item.title: Quaest: Lula tem 5 pontos à frente de Flávio Bolsonaro em Minas Gerais
item.description: A Quaest poll showed Lula (PT) leading voter intentions in Minas Gerais with 35%, five points ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), who scored 30%. The survey interviewed 1,506 voters between September 19 and 22, with a margin of error of three percentage points and was registered with the Electoral Justice.

item.title: A disputa Lula x Flávio entre eleitores de São Paulo, segundo a Quaest
item.description: Quaest survey shows technical tie between Flávio Bolsonaro (34%) and Lula (31%) in São Paulo, with a two-point margin of error. In a second round, Flávio maintains advantage (42% vs 36%), narrowing the gap since September.

item.title: MP contra bets acende alerta eleitoral no Planalto
item.description: The federal government plans to announce a provisional measure to tighten rules on online betting, driven by electoral data showing high usage among voters, particularly in the South and among Bolsonaro supporters. The MP, in advanced stages of discussion, includes restrictions on betting advertising and regulations for virtual casinos. A April survey shows 29% of Brazilians aged 16 or older bet online.

item.title: Quaest: em Minas, Lula e Flávio empatam com 40% cada no 2º turno
item.description: Quaest survey in Minas Gerais shows a tie between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro with 40% each in the second round. In the first round, Lula leads with 35% followed by Flávio with 30%. Minas is a strategic state in the presidential election.

item.title: Brasil tem 355 domínios de bets ilegais para cada autorizado, diz ANJL
item.description: The ANJL reports that Brazil has 355 illegal betting domains for every authorized one, with 66,482 sites blocked between January 2025 and September 2026. A ban on online casinos could increase the illegal market share from 41% to 80%, harming tax collection and player protection.
